title: Ordinary etale smooth purity with diagonal normalization
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $p:P\to X$ a smooth separated compactifiable morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On ordinary small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the right adjoint $p^!$ of ordinary $Rp_!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. With $\Lambda(1)=\mu_\ell\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell}\Lambda$, signed tensor powers as in [def-per-potential-dualizing], and $M(d)=M\otimes^L\Lambda(d)$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], there are natural isomorphisms
$$\gamma_{p,M}:p^*M(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}p^!M\qquad(M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)).$$
They commute with restriction to etale open charts, Noetherian change of base, and composition of smooth morphisms under the compact-support right-adjoint transitivity comparison. Their normalization is the diagonal-class orientation: on the affine line the first Chern class of the diagonal defines the duality unit and integration sends the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(1)$ to $1$; the deformation to the normal cone identifies the resulting dualizing line with the roots-of-unity Tate line. On affine $d$-space the orientation is the ordered tensor product of these affine-line orientations. For $d=0$ it is the etale inverse-image comparison. No perfect-field or finite-field hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Set $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ and $\omega_h=h^!A$. All adjoints below are the ordinary etale compact-support adjoints. Smoothness gives local finite presentation; compactifiability gives finite type and separatedness. A finite-type scheme over a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian. Base change preserves separatedness, finite type and smooth relative dimension. Thus $W=P\times_XP$, its projection $p_1:W\to P$ and diagonal $\Delta$ are admissible; $\Delta$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $d$, with normal bundle $T_{P/X}$. Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; Nagata supplies compactifications for all separated finite-type maps introduced below. In particular the normal-bundle projection and extended-Rees family in the section-specialization theorem are admissible. That theorem supplies smoothness, separatedness, finite type and Noetherianity of the deformation family. The same verifications apply after any Noetherian change of base. No ground field is introduced.

source.place: sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md: admissibility of the diagonal and section deformation

proof.text: Fix the affine normalization on a Noetherian base $S$. For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, use the supported diagonal Kummer class $\delta:R\Delta_*A\to A(1)[2]$. The ordinary projective-line adjunction has counit $\epsilon_{q,K}= (1_K\otimes t_q)\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$, with $t_qh=1$ for $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Its unit is the diagonal formula (G6): $M\simeq Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*M\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*M(1)[2]\simeq q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$. The two diagonal integrals are identities; these are exactly the two triangle identities in det-sp-p1-adjunction. Restricting this adjunction through $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$ gives the affine-line adjunction in lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace, whose unit therefore uses the restricted supported diagonal class. This is a supported class: forgetting support on $\mathbf A^2_S$ need not retain it. Iterating the line adjunction in the ordered coordinate tower defines the affine-$r$ comparison and trace, with the identity adjunction at $r=0$. This establishes the diagonal-class and integration normalization, not just an unspecified isomorphism.

proof.text:
The Cartesian square defining $p_1$ gives $p_2^*\omega_p\xrightarrow{\beta}\omega_{p_1}$ by ordinary smooth exceptional base change. Pulling back along $\Delta$ and using $p_2\Delta=1_P$ gives $a_p:\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$. Apply the normalized section deformation comparison to $(p_1,\Delta)$ to obtain $\delta_p:\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi$, where $\pi:T_{P/X}\to P$. Specialize vector-bundle purity to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $n=1$, so its coefficient ring is $A$. Its unit-coefficient comparison is $\Gamma_\pi:A(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\pi$. Define
$$\alpha_p=(z^*\Gamma_\pi^{-1})\delta_p a_p:\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}A_P(d)[2d].$$
The Tate line is precisely $\mu_\ell\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell}A$ by the ordinary Tate identification in vector-bundle purity. This fixes the specified diagonal, extended-Rees specialization and roots-of-unity orientation; it requires no perfectness assumption.

We compute this orientation on a smooth chart $h:U\to V$, with $V,U$ affine and $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ etale. Such charts exist by the smooth local normal form, and their opens are Noetherian. On $U\times_VU$, subtract the first-factor coordinates from the second-factor coordinates: $x_i=e_i(u_2)-e_i(u_1)$. This gives an etale map to $\mathbf A^d_U$ carrying the diagonal to zero. The inverse image of zero is etale separated over $U$, with the diagonal as a clopen section; remove its complementary closed component. Hence it is a map of section pairs with scheme-theoretic inverse image exactly the diagonal. Apply lem-per-etale-section-deformation-comparison: its two fibre comparisons identify $\delta_h$ with the identity in these coordinates, using the frame $[x_i]$ on the normal bundle. Vector integration in this frame is the ordered affine trace, by its definition. Finally etale locality and mate pasting identify $a_h$ with the counit-preserving chart comparison. Thus
$$\alpha_h=e^*(\Gamma_{p_d}^{-1})\circ E_e,\qquad E_e:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}e^*\omega_{p_d},$$
where $E_e$ is the canonical etale locality isomorphism and $\Gamma_{p_d}$ is the ordered affine comparison from Step 2. The normal frame is induced by coordinate differences, not chosen independently. The translation used here preserves the specified affine trace: in one coordinate $z\mapsto z-a$ extends to $[x_0:x_1]\mapsto[x_0-a x_1:x_1]$, fixes infinity and preserves the hyperplane line bundle. Its Kummer class and the unit summand in the projective-line decomposition are therefore preserved; the second-summand projection defining $t_q$ is preserved as well. Restriction gives the affine-line assertion, and successive coordinate translations give the ordered affine-space assertion. Thus subtracting first-factor coordinates changes neither counit nor orientation.

proof.text:
For any ordinary etale complex $M$, set
$$\gamma_{p,M}=\phi_{p,M}\circ(1\otimes\alpha_p^{-1}):p^*M(d)[2d]\to p^!M,$$
where $\phi$ is the canonical projection-and-counit tensor map. The tensor theorem makes $\phi$ an isomorphism on the entire ordinary derived category, and $\alpha_p$ is an isomorphism by Step 3. Thus $\gamma$ is an isomorphism, natural in $M$; restrict to $D^+$ as requested. On an affine chart its transpose is the etale sum counit followed by ordered affine integration. Indeed the affine-line counit has the projection-and-trace formula of Step 2; the tensor-composition identity rewrites its iterates as the projection map followed by the constant-coefficient composite counit, and the same identity with the etale chart functor inserts its sum counit. Uniqueness of counit-preserving right-adjoint comparison therefore identifies the resulting chart map with $\gamma$. This also checks that the tensor construction uses the actual affine normalization.

source.place: sk-thm-smooth-purity.proof.md: inverse orientation followed by canonical tensor map

proof.text: For a Noetherian base change $b:X'\to X$, write $b':P'\to P$ and $B:b'^*\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p'}$. The section-specialization theorem gives its normalized comparison after pullback; the diagonal square and its pullbacks give the same $a$ by mate pasting. Vector integration commutes with base change: on trivializations this is exactly $t_{p'_d}C_{d,b}=b^*t_{p_d}$ from the affine trace theorem, and its defining unique gluing gives the equality for every bundle. The vector comparison is its adjoint, so the same mate calculation identifies its pullback. Consequently the three factors of Step 3 give $\alpha_{p'}B=b'^*\alpha_p$ with the canonical Tate identifications. Now use the explicit tensor/base-change identity $\beta_{p,b,M}b'^*\phi_{p,M}=\phi_{p',b^*M}(1\otimes B)$ and substitute $\alpha_{p'}^{-1}=B(b'^*\alpha_p)^{-1}$. This gives $\beta_{p,b,M}b'^*\gamma_{p,M}=\gamma_{p',b^*M}$. For an etale source chart, Step 4 and the chart description in Step 5 give the restriction comparison. On overlaps these are maps of shifted locally free rank-one sheaves for the unit object; full faithfulness of the single-complex embedding and sheaf gluing ensure equality, rather than an invalid assertion about arbitrary derived morphisms being locally detectable.

source.place: sk-thm-dnc.proof.md: normalized gluing and change of base; sk-prop-an.proof.md: local integration and purity map

proof.text: For composable smooth maps $P\xrightarrow p X\xrightarrow q Y$ of dimensions $d,e$, compare the two maps into $(qp)^!M$ under the adjunction conjugate of $Rq_!Rp_!\simeq R(qp)_!$. The tensor-composition identity and the composite-counit formula reduce their equality to the equality of the unit-coefficient orientations. By the tensor theorem all unit-coefficient dualizing objects in this comparison are shifted rank-one sheaves, in degree $-2(d+e)$ after tensoring. Thus this equality can be checked on a cover using full faithfulness and sheaf gluing. Choose compatible charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$. The induced $U\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_T}=\mathbf A^{d+e}_T$ is etale, by etale base change and composition. By Steps 4 and 5 all comparisons are the counit-preserving comparisons of these chart adjunctions. Their counit is the sum over the etale fibres followed by integration in the $d$ coordinates, followed by integration in the $e$ coordinates. The ordered $(d+e)$-coordinate adjunction has exactly this counit: its Hom bijection is the same succession of the $d+e$ affine-line Hom bijections and the etale Hom bijections. The coherent compact-support composition and mate-pasting identities identify these with the prescribed transitivity comparison. Uniqueness of right-adjoint comparison gives equality on every chart, hence for the orientation globally, hence for all $M$ by the tensor reduction. Shift degrees are even, so reassociating twists introduces no Koszul sign.

proof.text: At $d=0$ the morphism is etale. Apply lem-pur-finite-smooth-gamma-normalization with $n=1$. Its three-factor $\alpha_p$ is exactly Step 3, including the canonical Rees-to-normal identification; its tensor composite is exactly Step 5. The resulting comparison is the counit-preserving etale inverse-image comparison, including for a nontrivial etale cover and for an open immersion. The identity and empty cases are included. Together with Step 2 this verifies every requested normalization and concludes the proof.
